function.name: locate_tallest_mountains

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency

message.content:
**Common proteins that reside in the plasma membrane** | Category | Example proteins (with brief function) | |----------|----------------------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** – pumps Na⁺ out and K⁺ in, maintaining membrane potential.
• **Voltage‑gated Na⁺ channel (Nav1.x)** – initiates action potentials in neurons.
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** – facilitates passive glucose uptake.
• **Aquaporin‑4 (AQP4)** – water channel in astrocytes and kidney.
• **β‑adrenergic receptor (GPCR)** – binds adrenaline, activates G‑protein signaling.
• **Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)** – tyrosine‑kinase receptor for EGF.
• **Integrin α5β1** – mediates cell–extracellular matrix adhesion. | | **Peripheral (surface‑associated) proteins** | • **GPI‑anchored protein CD59** – protects cells from complement‑mediated lysis.
• **Annexin A2** – binds phospholipids in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner, involved in membrane repair.
• **MHC class I molecules** – present peptides to cytotoxic T cells. | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | • **Src family kinases (e.g., Src)** – anchored via N‑terminal lipid modifications, regulate signaling.
• **Ras** – small GTPase attached to the inner leaflet, controls cell proliferation. | | **Channel and transporter families** | • **Kir (inward rectifier K⁺ channels)** – maintain resting membrane potential.
• **ClC chloride channels** – mediate Cl⁻ flux.
• **Sodium‑glucose cotransporter SGLT1** – co‑transport Na⁺ and glucose. | | **Receptor families** | • **Insulin receptor** – tyrosine‑kinase receptor for insulin.
• **Toll‑like receptor 4 (TLR4)** – recognizes LPS, initiates innate immune response.
• **Chemokine receptor CXCR4** – GPCR involved in chemotaxis. | | **Structural/adhesion proteins** | • **Cadherins (E‑cadherin)** – calcium‑dependent cell–cell adhesion.
• **Desmosomal proteins (desmoglein, desmoplakin)** – provide mechanical strength. | These proteins are just a snapshot of the diverse repertoire found in the plasma membrane. The exact composition varies by cell type and physiological state, but the above examples illustrate the major functional classes—ion channels, transporters, receptors, adhesion molecules, and signaling proteins—that are essential for cellular communication, transport, and structural integrity.
